source.source_diff: Only endpoint.rs differs across full production input manifests; namespace formatting moved once per scan, namespace directory comparison once per directory.

method.ratio: old measurement / new measurement per matched block; >1 favors new
method.median: Arithmetic midpoint of two central sorted values for n=8; ratio medians are medians of paired ratios, not ratios of medians.
method.p95: Nearest-rank ceil(0.95*n); for n=8 this is the observed maximum, not a stable population tail estimate.
method.primary_boundary: Before recipe/frame construction through validated Published and request-buffer destruction; includes handler and bounded instrumentation. Handler stages are subsets, never added again.
method.exclusions: Template preparation, synchronized clone, endpoint open, fixture generation, and reopened verification are separate costs. No network; frame bytes modeled.
method.outlier_policy: Retain all eight pairs, including slow process/row observations. No normalization by unchanged controls. No post-hoc substitute gate.

findings.detail: Neither P768 sparse policy reached 1.10 paired geometric mean. Normal policy met 6/8 wins; one-node policy reached only 4/8. No performance acceptance or WAN escalation from this result.
Normal sparse CPU old/new geometric mean 1.079686, paired median 1.044939, range 0.862452..1.655413. Raw CPU medians 41.1575ms old /39.902ms new. All pairs retained.
One-node sparse CPU geometric mean 1.037647, paired median 0.999308, range 0.945291..1.296429, 4/8 wins.
P768 raw normal total CPU ratio 0.914641 with 2/8 wins; Finish CPU ratio 0.873786 with 0/8 wins. Keep the regression; its cause is not isolated by these data.
P768 raw one-node total CPU ratio 1.129971 and 6/8 wins; wall ratio 0.965459. It does not replace the registered sparse gates.

Unchanged frame preparation varies materially: P768 normal sparse paired ratio 1.088912; block7 old prep 16.296ms vs new9.053ms, alongside old Finish37.501ms vs new17.032ms. Host one-minute load snapshots range5.99..23.63. No pairs deleted or results corrected after seeing data.

limitations: Local in-process instrumented diagnostic only: no WAN throughput or joule claim.
Eight pairs on one Mac; host background load, scheduling, power/thermal conditions and OS page cache were not controlled.
AB/BA and within-block ordering are balanced but do not eliminate nuisance variation or identify the cause of every observed regression.
Both graph cache retention knobs are zero. The one-node policy also changes admission/reservations and optional graph readiness; it is not a pure graph-compute on/off switch.
Raw normal Finish still prepares a canonical graph; sparse skips that step. Compare old/new within the same policy and mode.
Begin/Finish stages contain filesystem work, hashing and publication in addition to namespace formatting; no per-function profiler exists here.
Full filesystem scans remain O(number of cached publications); this change removes repeated formatting/comparison only.
Initial single-block baseline characterization is separate from the eight paired blocks and excluded from the paired effect estimate.
Quantiles and CPU-ratio estimates are descriptive; no statistical significance or population-level performance guarantee is claimed.
